How it works#

An IB Diploma with 24 points opens every programme in Denmark — if you also meet that programme's subject requirements.

Is it for you?
Why it might suit you#

No tuition at all for EU, EEA and Swiss citizens, and SU on top if you hold Danish citizenship or, as another EU/EEA citizen, gain equal status (in practice through part-time work).

All 5 reasons
What to watch for#

The deadline is 12:00 noon on 15 March, not midnight, and it applies to every IB holder including those who took the IB in Denmark.

All 5 things to watch
What it is actually like#
Getting in
How your IB is read#

The Agency converts your IB total to the Danish scale: 30 points is 6.9, 36 is 9.3, 40 is 10.7.

How it is used
How your subjects count#

HL generally becomes A level and SL becomes B — but not always, and the exceptions matter.

The exceptions
How and when you apply#

Applications close at 12:00 noon CET on 15 March 2027 — not midnight. Results come out on 6 July.

What happens after
How places are decided#

Quota 1 ranks on your converted average alone; quota 2 weighs other things. You are considered for both.

How the quotas work
Language#

The English-taught set is much smaller.

Money and life
Money#

Nothing for EU, EEA and Swiss citizens. Everyone else pays roughly €6,000–16,000 a year.

Living there#

Danish universities have no tradition of campus accommodation.

How it works#

Spain has a single gateway for IB students: an accreditation from UNED called UNEDasiss.

More on Spain
Is it for you?
Why it might suit you#

One digital accreditation (UNEDasiss) is accepted by most Spanish universities, so you do not repeat the paperwork for each one

All 5 reasons
What to watch for#

The timetable is tight for an IB student: the ordinary PCE exams in Spain (25–29 May in 2026) fall in the week straight after the May IB exams end (20 May in 2026), so you revise for both at once

All 5 things to watch
The shape of the system#

Degrees (grados) are taught at universidades, public or private.

The 4 routes in full
Getting in
How your IB is read#

Minimum: 24 points (the full IB Diploma pass). The minimum for an equivalent Spanish grade to be issued.

Subjects, levels and conversion
How and when you apply#

Where to apply: UNEDasiss (accreditation) then each region's preinscripción system

The 7 steps
Deadlines#

2 November 2026: Universidad de Deusto applications for 2027–2028

All 13 dates
Language#

A real but concentrated offer. Most English-taught bachelors sit at a handful of universities — IE, Carlos III, Pompeu Fabra, Navarra, ESADE, Autònoma de Barcelona, Deusto, Comillas — rather than being spread across the system.

Proving your English, and the rest
Money and life
Money#

Public universities charge per credit and the price is set regionally.

Fees, living costs and funding
Living there#

As an EU/EEA citizen you travel on your passport or national ID card.

Residency, work, housing and healthcare
If you are Spanish#

If you hold Spanish citizenship, you do not register a right of residence or prove your fee status, and Spain's own student grants and loans are open to you on their ordinary terms; check them, because some depend on where you have lived.
